_comment: sim-robust-portal-floor-seam-v1: MERGE this ONE top-level key into the mission runtime-config ON TOP of the PR258 (sim-robust-heading-hold-bound) + PR259 (sim-robust-throat-momentum-launch) navigation blocks -- keep ALL of those keys ON; this fragment does not replace them, it removes the geometry cause they were working around. WHY: the coupled outbound tow pins at x=-3.935 to the MILLIMETRE, from rest, while aligned (PR258 did its job), even with PR259 commanding a perfect dead-straight cruise (launch1b 2026-10-25: commanded straight=1 cruise 0.18 for 200+ ticks, base_yaw +-0.5 deg, yet zero advance for 27 s). A full CPU scan of the composed stage (mission.usda + the supermarket.usdc sublayer; AABB + actual mesh vertices + point-level nearest-collider + all floor/ground meshes + all decor) finds NO collider edge, seam, z-step, sill, rim, or physical decal at the pin -- the Backroom_floor is a single flat continuous slab, top z=0, and nothing else is within 0.25 m of any drive-wheel/caster/chassis probe. So the pin is NOT a modelled obstacle. ROOT CAUSE (CPU-measured): the Backroom_floor is a TRIANGLE-MESH collider (physics:approximation='none'); PhysX cooks its top quad into two triangles sharing one internal DIAGONAL edge, and on a flat floor that edge carries an in-plane (horizontal) contact normal -- exactly the 'vertical in-plane edge, no z climb, both drive wheels True, both casters airborne' the RESTOCK_TRACE_CASTERS trace shows. The cart's FRONT-LEFT swivel caster lands ON that cooked diagonal: measured perpendicular distance front-left caster -> diagonal = -0.002 m (launch1b), -0.014 m (coldwin18), +0.040 m (coldwin9) on every PINNED run, vs +0.238 m CLEAR on launch1a, the one run that crossed. The coupled train is rigid through the hitch: base_x = cart_x + (cart_hitch_x - hitch_x) = cart_x + 1.27, and the caster catches at a near-fixed cart pose (cart_x ~ -5.205), so the base halts at -5.205 + 1.27 = -3.935 to the millimetre -- the whole 7-run cluster. Momentum is NOT the discriminator (coldwin9 approached FASTER than the passer launch1a and still pinned); caster-on-edge is. FIX: author the flat drive floor as a BOX (boundingCube) collider -- six flat faces, NO internal edge -- so the casters roll across cleanly. Opt-in, default off => byte-identical triangle-mesh floor; the box slab is geometrically identical to the floor (same flat top z=0, same footprint), changes no visual/geometry/physics mass, and a flat floor SHOULD be a box not a triangle mesh (standard PhysX practice).
_integration_lane_steps: 1. Merge the single key "portal_floor_box": true at the TOP LEVEL of the mission runtime config (a scene-build key, like "visuals"/"cage_collision", NOT under "navigation"). The integration lane owns the ~/datasets configs; do NOT hand-edit them via a worker PR. Keep the PR258 + PR259 navigation blocks ON (they are the untouched backstop).
2. Confirm at boot: the console must print 'PORTAL_FLOOR_BOX enabled=True ...' from physics_setup. Absent/false => the floor stays a triangle mesh (byte-identical) and the pin can recur.
3. Set RESTOCK_TRACE_CASTERS=1 (caster swivel + wheel-contact proxy per nav-trace row) and keep RESTOCK_NAV_PLAN_DIAG=1 for the NAV_THROAT_LAUNCH / NAV_HEADING_HOLD console lines.

4. Bounded couple+outbound proof from the coldwin18 seat: run_mobile_restock.py --start-at couple --stop-after outbound, serialized through flock /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, HEAVY_MB=2500 if whispr holds VRAM, NEVER --force, never touch whispr (pid 1339, ~2.2 GB). Repeat THREE times.

5. Grade each run's nav-trace with the shipped gate: python3 scripts/check_tow_traction.py --environment <env.json> --scenario <mission-scenario.json> --camera-config <camera-config-bay.json> --fragment docs/examples/coupled-traction-fragment.json --runs-dir <mission-dir> --gpu-run <run-dir>. PASS (all THREE): GPU_RUN PASS, reached_goal=true (bay reached), crosses x=-3.90, single_tick_stops=0, trace_has_casters=true, and the console shows NO 'NAV_BREAKAWAY enter' and NO 'coupled_no_progress'. Then run scripts/check_portal_floor_seam.py --run <run-dir> on at least one PASS to confirm (as a cross-check) the front-caster-vs-diagonal evidence is gone / the floor is a box. Then the full capstone.

_key_notes.portal_floor_box: bool (or a truthy mapping {"enabled": true}); top-level scene-build key read by restock.scene.build -> compose.author_static_colliders(flat_floor_box=...). Default absent/false/None => the flat drive-floor meshes (twin.colliders.DRIVE_FLOOR_MESHES = {'Backroom_floor'}) stay triangle-mesh colliders (approximation 'none'), byte-identical to every prior run. True => those meshes get a box collider (approximation 'boundingCube'): the SAME flat slab with no internal triangulation edge, so the tow casters have nothing to ghost-collide at the portal. Only the flat drive floor is affected; every wall/shelf/ceiling/fixture stays a faithful triangle mesh. The whole outbound-to-bay path (x -4.5..-2.0, y ~15.3-15.45) stays on Backroom_floor, so this one mesh covers the bounded proof.

_scope_note: This fragment only re-approximates the flat drive-floor collider (triangle mesh -> box) to remove the PhysX internal-edge ghost contact; it does not touch PR207's drive force / caster_lift, PR241's lead-in, PR201's thresholds, PR236's bound, PR250's rock, PR258's heading-hold, PR259's momentum launch, the couple fine-dock, any cart mass / friction, and it never commands reverse. If the full capstone later tows onto the SALES floor (y<11; no real run has reached it yet), that slab (GRP_Structure/Floor) is also a triangle mesh with its own cooked diagonal -- extend DRIVE_FLOOR_MESHES then, as a follow-up. Full analysis + per-run caster-vs-diagonal numbers + the hitch arithmetic: data/sim-robust-portal-floor-seam-v1/report.md. CPU proof: scripts/check_portal_floor_seam.py, scripts/twin/tests/test_portal_floor_seam.py; policy twin/colliders.py (BOX / DRIVE_FLOOR_MESHES), authoring twin/compose.py (author_static_colliders flat_floor_box), wiring twin/restock/scene.py + physics_setup.py (portal_floor_box).
